relevant_files.relevance: Explicit rebuild scan/read/index work currently runs in the Electron main process.
Search request path can build an in-memory HNSW index when no committed artifact is available.
SQLite keyword rebuild is called synchronously from the main process.
Public Settings actions return quickly but still schedule heavy native work in the main process.
Full delete, tokenizer processing, and FTS inserts execute inside a synchronous better-sqlite3 transaction.
VACUUM and delete operations are synchronous and backup handling can miss WAL/SHM state.
Settings needs polling/action in-flight guards and clearer cancel-safe status UX.

missing_evidence: No automated event-loop responsiveness regression exists for active rebuild/compact.
No generation-swap test proves old SQLite keyword index remains searchable during failed rebuild.
No large-corpus temp-index benchmark artifact currently proves 200 MiB corpus behavior.
